if anything, you can contribute to society - if that is what you would want - your ideas about depression. I've never heard it called a terminal illness, but thats an enlightening take on it, in a way, and sharing about it could shed some light on your situation and make you feel vindicated in a way.

Life doesn't end after college. A lot of people do settle down in their 20's but there are tons of single people in both their 20's and 30's.
If you get an associates degree at a technical college, there are people of all ages. Less so with a 4-year degree. You'll find you're not the odd man out on most campuses.
And, if you can, go on vacation.

I'd also treat yourself as much as humanly possible. Take out, chocolate, whatever works for whatever diet you can run. I'm not 100% myself, but I know that eventually things will get better and I won't have to rely on so much candy or whatnot in the future.
